To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the absorptive capacity of knowledge brokers is a key factor to explain their ability to use external knowledge and 2) this absorptive capacity is composed of three main dimensions: the ability to recognize, the ability to assimilate and the ability to apply.
the absorptive capacity of brokers is a multidimensional construct, which is composed of three dimensions: knowledge acquisition, knowledge assimilation and knowledge transformation.

1) knowledge brokers working in Canadian health organizations have good absorptive capacity, 2) the absorptive capacity of knowledge brokers is positively correlated with their education level, their experience, their status in the organization and their membership to an association, and 3) the absorptive capacities of knowledge brokers are positively related to their use of research in their organization.
